# Canonical Golden Evidence

This closed inventory stores owner-approved direct firmware goldens by IC, workflow, variant or version, topology, and case. `provenance/case.json` normally pins every physical artifact by size, SHA-256, source facts, approval, original filename, and `legacyPaths` provenance. The sole narrow approved exception is the owner-certified neutral-name NT51929 input-only case: its original names and intake archive are prohibited from Git, so its case certification and exact artifact hashes replace those provenance fields.

Fact-scoped aliases contain no copied firmware payload. One direct case may bind one immutable physical input to multiple logical command roles, while different direct cases retain separate case inventories. Diagnostic controls and owner handoff material are classified by `testdata/diagnostics/golden-evidence/manifest.json` and are excluded from canonical regression and release reference payloads. After physical migration was frozen, the record keeps hash-pinned references to the existing repository-only quarantine paths instead of copying payloads.

Release redistribution is a separate, closed authority. `../release-canonical-v1.json` is the sole admission for the exact reviewed v1.1.2 snapshot: 25 Direct Goldens, one owner-certified input-only evidence case (`nt51929-certified-metadata-inputs-20260904`), and nine self-contained aliases. It independently pins this README plus every selected case manifest by exact-byte SHA-256; an alias is selected only when its exact same-workflow Direct Golden source is selected too. The NT51929 case contains only two neutral-named raw input observations and remains neither a Direct Golden, a Standard/AB input-output pair, an expected output, nor a parity/support/runtime claim. Two older input-only cases and their three dependent aliases remain repository-only. Selection never scans the canonical tree or `directEvidence`; unlisted diagnostics, owner handoff, CJK14/HackMD transfer material, archives, private/generated material, and nested archives are excluded. The selection does not promote runtime support or turn allowed-byte-difference evidence into full-output parity.

The selected provenance BAT and CONFIG are inert reference bytes only. Their hashes preserve evidence identity; no application, packager, smoke, processor registry, or external-tool registry may invoke or register them.

Every physical `.bin` filename identifies its case IC. Generic names such as `tp_bin.bin`, `dp-input.bin`, `flash.bin`, and `expected-output.bin` are forbidden even when the directory path supplies the missing context. When an owner filename does not already identify the same IC, canonical storage uses the short `<ic>-<artifact-id>.bin` form while preserving the original filename and legacy path in provenance.
